radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate | Date: 15 January 2025 | Facility: Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)
Clinical indication: Evaluation of rising PSA (6.9 ng/mL) and clinical suspicion of malignancy.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 43.34 mL in volume. T2-weighted sequences demonstrate a focal hypointense area within the right posterior peripheral zone at the base, spanning approximately 18 x 14 x 16 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows marked restricted diffusion, mirrored by corresponding low signal on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, focal enhancement relative to surrounding parenchyma. No extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion is observed. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous lesions are seen.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right posterior peripheral zone.
PSAD 0.159 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.7682602.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: During a routine health screening in April 2023, a PSA reading of 3.7 ng/mL was recorded. The individual noted mild urinary frequency but explicitly denied pelvic discomfort or haematuria. A subsequent test was planned for later that year to track progression.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: A June 2024 follow-up test indicated an increase to 6.6 ng/mL. Considering the upward trajectory alongside his age, the urology department coordinated a multiparametric MRI.
